questions.question: AB is parallel to CD. A transversal PQ intersects AB and CD at E and F, respectively, and ∠PEB = 49°. G is a point between AB and CD such that ∠BEG = 35° and ∠GFE = 16°. What is the measure of ∠EGF?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since **AB || CD**, the **linear pair** at point E gives ∠FEB = 180° − 49° = 131°.

The interior angle ∠FEG = ∠FEB − ∠BEG = 131° − 35° = 96°.

In **▵EFG**, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠EGF = 180° − (∠FEG + ∠GFE) = 180° − (96° + 16°) = 68°.

**∴ The correct answer is 68°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Line **AB || CD**, transversal **PQ** intersects them at E and F.

∠PEB = 49°, ∠BEG = 35°, and ∠GFE = 16°.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Linear Pair Axiom:** Sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

2. **Angle Sum Property:** Sum of angles in a triangle is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d348b68bfe55688188bd6bd1fbd9732b10acc22425996638827d90350006367.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since P-E-F-Q is a straight line, ∠PEB + ∠FEB = 180°

⇒ 49° + ∠FEB = 180°

⇒ ∠FEB = 180° − 49° = 131°

⇒ From the figure, ∠FEB = ∠FEG + ∠BEG

⇒ 131° = ∠FEG + 35°

⇒ ∠FEG = 131° − 35° = 96°

⇒ In **▵EFG**, ∠EGF + ∠FEG + ∠GFE = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF + 96° + 16° = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF + 112° = 180°

⇒ ∠EGF = 180° − 112° = 68°

**∴ The correct answer is 68°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines and Transversals

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, **alternate interior angles** are equal, and **consecutive interior angles** are supplementary (sum to 180°).

Triangle Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180°.

Linear Pair of Angles

A linear pair is a set of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines; their measures always add up to 180°.</p

questions.question: 9 men or 8 women can do a job in 19 days. 9 men work for 9 days and leave. The number of women required to complete the remaining work in 8 days is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work in terms of **men-days** = 9 × 19 = 171 units.

Work done by 9 men in 9 days = 9 × 9 = 81 units.

Remaining work = 171 − 81 = 90 units (to be done by women).

Since 9 men = 8 women, 171 men-days = 8 × 19 = 152 women-days.

Ratio of Men work to Women work is 8 : 9. Remaining work for women = 90 × (8/9) = 80 women-days.

Number of women needed for 8 days = 80 ÷ 8 = 10 women.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 9 Men 19 8 
 8 Women 19 152 8 

**Given:** 9 men or 8 women can do a job in 19 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Efficiency of 9 men = 152 ÷ 19 = 8 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 8 women = 152 ÷ 19 = 8 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 1 woman = 8 ÷ 8 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Work done by 9 men in 9 days = 8 × 9 = 72 units

⇒ Remaining work = 152 − 72 = 80 units

⇒ Women required to finish 80 units in 8 days = 80 ÷ (8 × 1) = 10 women

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Additional Information__**

The 'OR' Concept in Work

When a question says 'A or B', it implies that the total capacity of group A is equal to the total capacity of group B (m₁d₁ = m₂d₂).

Work & Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If the same work is done in fewer days, the efficiency of the group must be higher.

Man-Day Formula

M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is number of workers, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 7 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 56 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill three-fourth of the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = **Inlet** efficiency − **Outlet** efficiency

Efficiency of **Pipe 1** = 56 ÷ 7 = 8 units/min

Efficiency of **Pipe 2** = 56 ÷ 56 = 1 unit/min

Combined efficiency = 8 − 1 = 7 units/min

Time for 3/4th tank = (3/4 × 56) ÷ 7 = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 7 min
 56 units
 8

 Pipe 2 (Empty)
 56 min

Given: **Filling Pipe** time = 7 min, **Emptying Pipe** time = 56 min

Formula Used: **Total Work** = **Efficiency** × **Time**

⇒ Let **Total Capacity** of tank = LCM(7, 56) = 56 units

⇒ Combined Efficiency of both pipes = 8 − 1 = 7 units/min

⇒ Target volume to fill = 3/4 × 56 = 42 units

⇒ Required Time = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipe efficiency is taken as positive (+), while outlet (leakage) pipe efficiency is taken as negative (−).

Net Work Done

If two pipes fill a tank in x and y hours, net work in 1 hour = 1/x + 1/y. If one fills and one empties, net work = 1/x − 1/y.</p

questions.question: The irrigation method in India that distributes water through pipes under low pressure to each plant is called:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Localised Irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Localised Irrigation**, also referred to as **micro-irrigation**, involves delivering water directly to the root zone of plants through a network of pipes under **low pressure**.
 
• This method is highly **efficient** as it reduces water wastage and ensures that plants receive the required amount of water directly at their roots.
 
• It is commonly used in **arid and semi-arid regions** where water scarcity is a significant concern.
 
• There are different forms of localised irrigation, including **drip irrigation** and **sprinkler irrigation**.
 
• Drip irrigation is particularly effective for crops like fruits, vegetables, and cash crops, ensuring uniform water distribution.
 
• Localised irrigation reduces water loss due to **evaporation, runoff, and deep percolation**.
 
• It promotes water conservation and enhances **crop productivity**, making it a sustainable irrigation method.
 
• The **Government of India** promotes this method under initiatives such as the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)** to encourage farmers to adopt efficient irrigation techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Furrow Irrigation**__

 __
 
• **Furrow irrigation** involves creating small parallel channels along the field through which water flows to irrigate crops.
 
• It is a **traditional irrigation method** and is commonly used for crops like maize, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
• This method is less efficient as it can lead to **water wastage** due to evaporation and runoff.
 
 
 
• **Tubewell Irrigation**__
 __
 
• **Tubewell irrigation** involves extracting groundwater using tubewells and pumps.
 
• It is widely used in regions with **ample groundwater availability**, such as Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Though effective, it can lead to the **depletion of groundwater resources** if not managed sustainably.
 
 
 
• **Canal Irrigation**__
 
 
• **Canal irrigation** is a method where water is transported from reservoirs or rivers through canals to agricultural fields.
 
• This method is extensively used in regions like the **Indo-Gangetic plains**.
 
• It requires **large-scale infrastructure** and is suitable for areas with abundant surface water.

questions.question: The average weight of 10 boys is 70 kg. But later, it was found that at two places the weight 54 kg was read as 44 kg and at one place weight 35 kg was read as 40 kg. Find the correct average weight (in kg) of the 10 boys.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change in **Total Sum** = (Correct Values − Incorrect Values)

Net change = [2 × (54 − 44)] + [1 × (35 − 40)] = 20 − 5 = +15 kg

Correction in **Average** = Net Change ÷ Number of Boys = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 kg

**Correct Average** = Old Average + Correction = 70 + 1.5 = 71.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 71.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **boys** (n) = 10

Initial **average weight** = 70 kg

Incorrect observations: 44 kg (twice) and 40 kg (once)

Correct observations: 54 kg (twice) and 35 kg (once)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/650c9324d9649bdfc9ee535345efc1711a8f36d8b248f2868b5b5be77bb1a3f0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Initial Weight = 10 × 70 = 700 kg

⇒ Sum of correct weights = (54 × 2) + 35 = 108 + 35 = 143 kg

⇒ Sum of incorrect weights = (44 × 2) + 40 = 88 + 40 = 128 kg

⇒ Correct Total Weight = 700 − 128 + 143 = 715 kg

⇒ Correct Average Weight = 715 ÷ 10 = 71.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 71.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Correction in Mean

When one or more observations are misread, the correct mean is: New Mean = Old Mean + [(Sum of Correct Values − Sum of Incorrect Values) ÷ n].

Sum of Observations

Total Sum = Average × Number of Observations. This is the base for finding corrections in total weight or marks.

Weighted Average

Used when combining two groups: Combined Avg = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is count and x is average.</p

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 78, 56, 52, 45, 97, 19, 37, 46 and 74 is:

Calculate **deviations** from 50: +28, +6, +2, −5, +47, −31, −13, −4, +24.

Sum of deviations = 28 + 6 + 2 − 5 + 47 − 31 − 13 − 4 + 24 = 54.

Net Adjustment = Sum of deviations ÷ Number of observations = 54 ÷ 9 = 6.

Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + Adjustment = 50 + 6 = 56.

**Given:** Observations are 78, 56, 52, 45, 97, 19, 37, 46, and 74.

**Formula Used:** **Arithmetic Mean** = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

⇒ Total number of **observations** (n) = 9

⇒ **Sum** = 78 + 56 + 52 + 45 + 97 + 19 + 37 + 46 + 74

Properties of Arithmetic Mean

The **sum of deviations** of items from their **Arithmetic Mean** is always **zero**: Σ(x − Mean) = 0.

Change in Origin and Scale

If each observation is increased by **k**, the mean increases by **k**. If each is multiplied by **k**, the mean is multiplied by **k**.

Mean of Natural Numbers

The mean of the first **n** natural numbers is calculated using the formula: **(n + 1) ÷ 2**.</p

questions.question: A certain number is divided into two parts such that 5 times the first part added to 14 times the second part makes 7 times the whole. The ratio of the second part to the first part is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using **Alligation Method** to find the ratio of parts:

First part weight = 5, Second part weight = 14, Average (Whole) weight = 7.

Ratio = (14 − 7) : (7 − 5) = 7 : 2 (First : Second).

The required ratio of **Second part to First part** is 2 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 5 × First part + 14 × Second part = 7 × (First part + Second part)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ece123c56c8380623a5f7da59e017ababc46ae62730e82945f6e5e5128730471.png] 

Let the first part be **x** and the second part be **y**.

⇒ 5x + 14y = 7(x + y)

⇒ 5x + 14y = 7x + 7y

⇒ 14y − 7y = 7x − 5x

⇒ 7y = 2x

⇒ y/x = 2/7

⇒ y : x = 2 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

Used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices/weights must be mixed to produce a mixture at a given mean price/weight. Ratio = (Higher Value − Mean) : (Mean − Lower Value).

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio compares two quantities by division. In an equation ax = by, the ratio x : y is equal to b : a.</p

questions.question: Mohan invests a sum of ₹5,000 and Varun invests a sum of ₹9,000 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 3 years, Varun gets ₹480 more interest than Mohan, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Principal** = ₹9,000 − ₹5,000 = ₹4,000.

Interest **difference** per year = ₹480 ÷ 3 = ₹160.

**Rate %** = (Yearly Interest Difference ÷ Principal Difference) × 100.

Rate = (160 ÷ 4,000) × 100 = 4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal for **Mohan** (PM) = ₹5,000

Principal for **Varun** (PV) = ₹9,000

Time (T) = **3 years**

Difference in interest (Idᵢff) = **₹480**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e23ea866e506c777c096eb629c88f9f1dd0e7253145861e71c2dcd6b3fa6f179.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **rate of interest** be R% per annum.

⇒ Interest for Varun − Interest for Mohan = 480

⇒ [(9,000 × R × 3) / 100] − [(5,000 × R × 3) / 100] = 480

⇒ [270 × R] − [150 × R] = 480

⇒ 120 × R = 480

⇒ R = 480 ÷ 120

⇒ R = 4%

**∴ The correct answer is 4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount for the entire duration. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

Interest Difference Property

When rate and time are constant, the difference in interest is directly proportional to the difference in principal: Idᵢff = (Pdᵢff × R × T) / 100.

Amount Calculation

Total Amount (A) returned at the end of the term is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest: A = P + SI.

questions.question: In the context of file systems, what is the primary purpose of a file system 'metadata'?

options.text: To define the graphical representation of files and folders for the user
To record information about the files and directories, such as their names, sizes, timestamps and permissions
To optimise the physical storage of file data on the storage device for faster access
To store the actual content and data of the files

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To record information about the files and directories, such as their names, sizes, timestamps, and permissions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **file system metadata** is essential for managing and organizing files and directories on a storage device.
 
• It includes vital information such as the **names, sizes, timestamps (creation, modification, and access times), and permissions** associated with each file and directory.
 
• **Metadata** enables the operating system to locate and access files efficiently, ensuring proper functioning of the file system.
 
• This data is typically stored in specialized structures such as **inodes** (in UNIX-like systems) or **Master File Tables (MFT)** (in NTFS).
 
• It also contains information about the **file structure** (e.g., whether a file is a regular file, directory, or symbolic link).
 
• By maintaining this data, the file system can enforce **security measures** (permissions and access controls) and enable features like **file versioning** or recovery.
 
• Efficient **metadata management** is crucial for system performance, as it directly impacts how quickly files can be located and accessed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To define the graphical representation of files and folders for the user**__

 __
 
• This option refers to the **user interface** of a file system, which is not the primary function of metadata.
 
• The graphical representation is determined by the **operating system’s file explorer**, such as Windows Explorer or macOS Finder.
 
• While metadata supports file organization, it does not dictate how files and folders appear visually to users.
 
 
 
• **To optimise the physical storage of file data on the storage device for faster access**__
 __
 
• This function falls under **data allocation algorithms** used by the file system to manage physical storage.
 
• Examples include **contiguous allocation, linked allocation, and indexed allocation**.
 
• While metadata can assist in tracking storage blocks, optimization of physical storage is a separate function.
 
 
 
• **To store the actual content and data of the files**__
 
 
• Metadata does not store the **actual file content**; it only describes and tracks the files.
 
• The **actual data** is stored in data blocks or clusters managed by the file system.
 
• Metadata acts as a reference guide, pointing to the location of these data blocks.

questions.question: A dealer marks his goods 65% above the cost price and allows a discount of 8% on the marked price. What is his gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change formula: **Net Gain% = a + b + (ab ÷ 100)**

Here, a = 65 (markup is positive) and b = −8 (discount is negative).

Gain% = 65 − 8 − (65 × 8 ÷ 100) = 57 − 5.2 = 51.8%.

Since the result is positive, it is a **gain**.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.8% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup = 65%, Discount = 8%.
**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Gain% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c6e875d1360cc17bcf1ca8ef22e3f4b85211d3dbf20e42dffa2f0cf82645cc5.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 65% of 100 = 165.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 165 − 8% of 165 = 165 × 0.92 = 151.8.

⇒ **Gain** = SP − CP = 151.8 − 100 = 51.8.

⇒ **Gain%** = (51.8 ÷ 100) × 100 = 51.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.8% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Profit or loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**.

Markup Percentage

Markup% = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It represents the increase in price over the base cost.</p

questions.question: The mean proportional between (11 + 5√2) and (9 - 5√2).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Mean proportional between **a** and **b** is given by **√(a × b)**.

Let a = (11 + 5√2) and b = (9 − 5√2).

Product = 11 × 9 − 11 × 5√2 + 9 × 5√2 − (5√2)² = 99 − 55√2 + 45√2 − 50 = 49 − 10√2.

Mean Proportional = √(49 − 10√2).

**∴ The correct answer is √(49 − 10√2).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = (11 + 5√2)

Second term (b) = (9 − 5√2)

**Formula Used:**

Mean proportional (M.P.) = √(a × b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ac8fc3d910c07e9fa2a7c807db1582f68ca1f97a80c0a64874f1f0330cef786.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ M.P. = √[(11 + 5√2) × (9 − 5√2)]

⇒ M.P. = √[11(9 − 5√2) + 5√2(9 − 5√2)]

⇒ M.P. = √[99 − 55√2 + 45√2 − 25(2)]

⇒ M.P. = √[99 − 10√2 − 50]

⇒ M.P. = √(49 − 10√2)

**∴ The correct answer is √(49 − 10√2).**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **x** and **y** is a number **z** such that x:z = z:y, which implies **z² = xy** or **z = √(xy)**.

Third Proportional

For two numbers **a** and **b**, the third proportional **c** is defined as a:b = b:c, giving **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c**, the fourth proportional **d** is defined as a:b = c:d, giving **d = (b × c)/a**.</p

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT contribute much to the degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Increased plantation of native trees**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Increased plantation of native trees** is a sustainable practice and contributes to the **restoration** of the ecosystem.
 
• Native trees are well-adapted to the **climatic conditions** and soil types of the region, making them ideal for conserving the **local biodiversity.**
 
• Planting native species enhances the ability of the Thar Desert to combat **desertification**, as these trees can provide shade, prevent soil erosion, and improve soil moisture retention.
 
• These trees support the local **wildlife** by providing habitats and food sources, and they also preserve the ecosystem's **natural balance.**
 
• Unlike invasive species, native trees do not disrupt the existing ecological processes. Instead, they contribute to the **stability** and resilience of the environment.
 
• Efforts to plant native trees are often part of **governmental and non-governmental programs** aimed at combating desertification under initiatives such as the **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD).**
 
• This practice does not lead to any significant degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem but rather helps in its **long-term sustainability.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Grazing by livestock**__

 __
 
• **Grazing by livestock** is a major contributor to the degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem. Overgrazing leads to **soil erosion** and the destruction of vegetation, which are critical to maintaining the desert’s delicate ecological balance.
 
• Livestock grazing often reduces the availability of **native vegetation**, leading to the loss of habitat for local wildlife.
 
• Excessive grazing also disrupts the soil’s capacity to retain moisture, further exacerbating **desertification.**
 
 
 
• **Erratic rainfall**__
 __
 
• **Erratic rainfall** is another factor impacting the Thar Desert ecosystem. The desert region experiences highly unpredictable and irregular rainfall patterns, which affect the **growth of vegetation** and the availability of water resources.
 
• Sudden bursts of rainfall can lead to **soil erosion**, while prolonged drought periods can decrease the survival rate of plants and animals.
 
• This variability in precipitation is a natural characteristic of desert climates but becomes more pronounced with **climate change.**
 
 
 
• **Climate change**__
 
 
• **Climate change** has a profound impact on the Thar Desert ecosystem, as rising temperatures and changing precipitation patterns intensify **desertification.**
 
• It leads to increased occurrences of **extreme weather events**, such as heatwaves and heavy storms, which disrupt the ecological balance.
 
• Climate change also affects the survival of **native flora and fauna**, as they struggle to adapt to the rapidly changing conditions.
 
• Global efforts to mitigate climate change, such as the **Paris Agreement**, aim to address these challenges to ecosystems worldwide, including the Thar Desert.

questions.question: When 1278, 2368 and 4318 are divided by the greatest number x, the remainder in each case is y. What is the value of (3x − 14y)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the same remainder **y**, **x** is the **HCF** of differences: |2368 − 1278|, |4318 − 2368|, and |4318 − 1278|.

Differences are 1090, 1950, and 3040. Their **HCF (x)** is 10.

Remainder **y** = 1278 ÷ 10 → **y = 8**.

Required value = 3(10) − 14(8) = 30 − 112 = −82.

**∴ The correct answer is -82.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08b54e31b376dd9aaefef096d026ebea699b7811786c108bc47abb6d38723fcd.png] 

**Given:** Numbers are 1278, 2368, 4318.

**Step 1:** Calculate differences between numbers:

⇒ 2368 − 1278 = 1090

⇒ 4318 − 2368 = 1950

⇒ 4318 − 1278 = 3040

**Step 2:** Find **x** (HCF of 1090, 1950, 3040):

⇒ 1090 = 10 × 109

⇒ 1950 = 10 × 195

⇒ 3040 = 10 × 304

⇒ Common factor **x = 10**.

**Step 3:** Find remainder **y**:

⇒ 1278 = (10 × 127) + 8

⇒ **y = 8**.

**Step 4:** Calculate (3x − 14y):

⇒ 3(10) − 14(8) = 30 − 112 = −82.

**∴ The correct answer is -82.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF with Same Remainder

When **n** numbers are divided by the greatest number **x** to leave the same remainder, **x** is always the **HCF** of the absolute differences of those numbers.

HCF with Different Remainders

If numbers N₁, N₂, N₃ leave remainders r₁, r₂, r₃, then the greatest divisor is **HCF((N₁−r₁), (N₂−r₂), (N₃−r₃))**.

Property of HCF

The **HCF** of any two numbers also divides their difference, which is why the difference method works for finding the greatest common divisor.</p

questions.question: The average weight of 14 boys in a class is 40.25 kg and that of the remaining 4 boys is 33.5 kg. Find the average weight (in kg, rounded off to two decimal place) of all the boys in the class.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **number of boys** = 14 : 4 = 7 : 2.

Using **Deviation Method**: Assume a base average of 33.5 kg.

Positive deviation from 7 units = 7 × (40.25 − 33.5) = 7 × 6.75 = 47.25.

Net increase in average = Total deviation ÷ Total units = 47.25 ÷ (7 + 2) = 5.25 kg.

Actual **average weight** = 33.5 + 5.25 = 38.75 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 38.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of boys (Group 1) = 14 | Average weight (Group 1) = 40.25 kg

Number of boys (Group 2) = 4 | Average weight (Group 2) = 33.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/868d77bd1baa98d41acb3736c8867e4167a5139968cf794906df5515c554b234.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of 14 boys = 14 × 40.25 = 563.5 kg

⇒ Total weight of 4 boys = 4 × 33.5 = 134 kg

⇒ Total weight of all 18 boys = 563.5 + 134 = 697.5 kg

⇒ Average weight of all boys = 697.5 ÷ 18

⇒ Average weight = 38.75 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 38.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When data is given in groups, the overall average is Aw = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂ + ... + nₖaₖ) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ... + nₖ).

Ratio Shortcut

If the number of items in groups can be simplified into a **ratio**, use the simplified ratio values instead of actual numbers for faster calculation.

Effect of Change in Each Term

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the average of the set also increases or decreases by **k**.

Properties of Average

The average always lies between the minimum and maximum values of the data set (i.e., 33.5 < 38.75 < 40.25).</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
To be divisible by **8**, the **last three digits** of the number must be divisible by 8.

Check options: (1) 370 → No, (2) 208 → Yes (208 ÷ 8 = 26), (3) 702 → No, (4) 659 → No.

Only **14208** satisfies the divisibility rule for 8.

Verify for 37: 14208 ÷ 37 = 384.

**∴ The correct answer is 14208.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Step 1: Divisibility by 8**

⇒ 15370: Last 3 digits 370 ÷ 8 → Remainder = 2 (Not divisible)

⇒ 14208: Last 3 digits 208 ÷ 8 → 26 (Divisible)

⇒ 13702: Last 3 digits 702 ÷ 8 → Remainder = 6 (Not divisible)

⇒ 15659: Last digit is odd (Not divisible)

**Step 2: Divisibility by 37 for 14208**

⇒ 14208 = (14800 − 592)

⇒ 14800 ÷ 37 = 400

⇒ 592 ÷ 37 = 16

⇒ 14208 ÷ 37 = 400 − 16 = 384 (Divisible)

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if its **last three digits** are zeros or form a number divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 37

For larger numbers, 37 has a property where **111, 222, 333...** are all divisible by 37 (since 37 × 3 = 111).

LCM Method

If a number is divisible by two **co-prime** numbers a and b, it must be divisible by their product (a × b). Here, 37 and 8 are co-prime.</p

questions.question: The Great Plateau of India is a part of which ancient landmass?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gondwana Land**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gondwana Land** was a part of the supercontinent **Pangaea**, which existed during the **Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras.**
 
• It comprised the present-day landmasses of **South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• The breakup of Gondwana Land led to the formation of the **continents as we know them today.**
 
• The **Great Plateau of India**, which includes the Deccan Plateau, is considered a part of Gondwana Land due to its **geological history and the presence of ancient rocks.**
 
• Gondwana rocks in India contain **coal deposits** and are significant for **mineral extraction**.
 
• The breakup of Gondwana Land is attributed to **tectonic plate movements and continental drift.**
 
• Its name is derived from the **Gondwana region** in India, which was identified as having rocks and fossils from this ancient landmass.
 
• Gondwana Land played a crucial role in the **evolution of life**, with fossils of early plants and animals found in its deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Angaraland**__

 __
 
• **Angaraland** was the northern counterpart of Gondwana Land, forming the other part of the supercontinent **Pangaea**.
 
• It consisted of present-day **Russia, Siberia, and parts of northern Europe.**
 
• Angaraland was separated from Gondwana Land by the **Tethys Sea**, which existed during the Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras.
 
• It played a significant role in the **geological evolution** of the northern hemisphere.
 
 
 
• **Pangaea**__
 __
 
• **Pangaea** was a supercontinent that existed during the **late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic eras.**
 
• It encompassed all of Earth's landmasses before they split into **Laurasia** and **Gondwana Land.**
 
• Pangaea's breakup led to the formation of the continents due to **tectonic plate movements.**
 
• The term "Pangaea" means "all lands" in Greek, highlighting its unified landmass.
 
 
 
• **Laurasia**__
 
 
• **Laurasia** was the northern part of the supercontinent **Pangaea** after its division.
 
• It included the modern landmasses of **North America, Europe, and Asia.**
 
• Laurasia's separation from Gondwana Land marked the **beginning of continental drift.**
 
• It contributed to the formation of the northern hemisphere continents and their geological features.

questions.question: Which of the following measures the percentage of a country's population living below the poverty line?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Poverty Headcount Ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Poverty Headcount Ratio** is a metric used to measure the percentage of a country's population that lives below the **poverty line**.
 
• This indicator helps in understanding the **extent of poverty** in a nation and is widely used in **social and economic analysis**.
 
• It is based on defining a specific **poverty threshold or line**, which represents the minimum income or consumption level required to meet basic needs such as **food, shelter, and clothing**.
 
• The **Poverty Headcount Ratio** is expressed as a percentage of the total population. For example, if 20% of a country's population lives below the poverty line, the ratio is 20%.
 
• This measure is crucial for governments and international organizations like the **World Bank** to assess the impact of their **poverty alleviation programs** and make informed policy decisions.
 
• It is often calculated using data from **household surveys** conducted at national and regional levels.
 
• The indicator is part of broader frameworks like the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically under Goal 1: No Poverty.
 
• The measure also provides insights into **inequality** and helps target resources toward the most vulnerable groups in society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Gini Coefficient**__

 __
 
• The **Gini Coefficient** is a measure of **income inequality** within a population.
 
• It ranges from **0** (perfect equality) to **1** (maximum inequality).
 
• A lower Gini Coefficient indicates a more **equal income distribution**, whereas a higher value suggests greater inequality.
 
• This metric is often used alongside poverty measures to understand the broader economic disparities in a society.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate**__
 __
 
• The **Unemployment Rate** refers to the percentage of the **labor force** that is unemployed but actively seeking work.
 
• This indicator highlights the **employment situation** in a country but does not directly measure poverty.
 
• It is an important economic metric but does not account for individuals who are **employed but still live in poverty** (working poor).
 
 
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**__
 
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite index that measures a country's overall **social and economic development**.
 
• It considers factors such as **life expectancy, education level, and per capita income**.
 
• Although HDI reflects development levels, it does not specifically measure the **proportion of people living in poverty**.

questions.question: If 2 is added to each odd digit and 1 is subtracted from each even digit in the number 2645783, what will be the sum of the highest and lowest digits in the new number thus formed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Original number = 2645783

For each digit in the number:

 
• Add 2 to each odd digit.
 
• Subtract 1 from each even digit.

**Formula Used:**

New digit = Odd digit + 2 (if digit is odd)

New digit = Even digit − 1 (if digit is even)

Sum of the highest and lowest digits = Highest digit in the new number + Lowest digit in the new number

**Calculation:**

Original number = 2, 6, 4, 5, 7, 8, 3

Step 1: Apply the transformation rule:

 
• 2 (even) ⇒ 2 − 1 = 1
 
• 6 (even) ⇒ 6 − 1 = 5
 
• 4 (even) ⇒ 4 − 1 = 3
 
• 5 (odd) ⇒ 5 + 2 = 7
 
• 7 (odd) ⇒ 7 + 2 = 9
 
• 8 (even) ⇒ 8 − 1 = 7
 
• 3 (odd) ⇒ 3 + 2 = 5

New number = 1, 5, 3, 7, 9, 7, 5

Step 2: Find the highest and lowest digits:

 
• Highest digit = 9
 
• Lowest digit = 1

Step 3: Calculate the sum of the highest and lowest digits:

⇒ Sum = 9 + 1

⇒ Sum = 10

**The sum of the highest and lowest digits in the new number is 10.**

questions.question: Which event marked the final collapse of the British policy of annexation?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Revolt of 1857**, also known as the **First War of Indian Independence**, marked a turning point in the history of British rule in India.
 
• It was a widespread but unsuccessful rebellion against the **British East India Company** rule.
 
• The revolt was triggered due to various factors such as **economic exploitation, political annexation, religious interference, and social injustices**.
 
• One of the key policies that fueled resentment was the **Doctrine of Lapse**, implemented by Lord Dalhousie, which allowed the British to annex Indian princely states if the rulers did not have a direct heir.
 
• The annexation of states like **Awadh** further intensified the discontent among Indian rulers and the local population.
 
• The rebellion was led by figures such as **Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, Tantia Tope, Nana Sahib**, and others, who became symbols of resistance.
 
• The revolt demonstrated the widespread dissatisfaction among Indians and revealed the **limitations of the British policies of annexation**.
 
• After suppressing the revolt, the British Crown took direct control of India through the **Government of India Act, 1858**, ending the era of East India Company rule.
 
• The revolt marked the final collapse of the British annexation policy, and subsequent rulers adopted a more cautious approach towards governance and administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Partition of Bengal**__

 __
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** in 1905 by Lord Curzon was a significant event in Indian history. It divided Bengal into **East Bengal and West Bengal** based on religious and administrative reasons.
 
• The move was seen as an attempt to divide Hindus and Muslims and weaken the nationalist movement.
 
• The widespread protests against the partition led to the growth of the **Swadeshi Movement** and ultimately resulted in the reversal of the partition in 1911.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement**__
 __
 
• The **Quit India Movement** was launched by the Indian National Congress on **8 August 1942** under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It demanded an end to British rule in India and was characterized by widespread protests, strikes, and civil disobedience.
 
• Unlike the Revolt of 1857, this movement was non-violent but still faced brutal suppression by the British authorities.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**__
 
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** was the longest Act passed by the British Parliament concerning India.
 
• It introduced significant reforms, including the establishment of provincial autonomy and the creation of the **Federal Court**.
 
• This Act laid the foundation for the federal structure of governance but did not address the complete independence aspirations of Indians.

questions.question: Let AB and CD be two parallel lines and PQ be a transversal, such that PQ intersects AB at the point R and CD at the point S. If ∠ARP = 2x°, ∠ARQ = y° and ∠DSP = 4x°, then find the values of x and y, respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **PQ** is a straight line, **∠ARP** and **∠ARQ** form a **linear pair**, so 2x + y = 180.

For **parallel lines** **AB** and **CD**, the **exterior angle** ∠ARP and the **interior angle** ∠RSD are **corresponding angles** (thus equal).

Since **∠RSD** and **∠DSP** form a **linear pair** at point **S**, their sum is 180°.

Substituting **∠ARP** for **∠RSD**: 2x + 4x = 180 ⇒ 6x = 180 ⇒ **x = 30**.

Now, 2(30) + y = 180 ⇒ 60 + y = 180 ⇒ **y = 120**.

**∴ The correct answer is 30; 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**AB || CD** and **PQ** is a **transversal**.

∠ARP = 2x°, ∠ARQ = y°, and ∠DSP = 4x°.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Linear Pair Axiom:** Sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

2. **Corresponding Angles Postulate:** If two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, then the pairs of corresponding angles are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67166ceacd95e7441b95b3afbd31eb6d4d84c635d66cd35ef4be2b9cc1484f73.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since **P-R-Q** is a straight line, ∠ARP + ∠ARQ = 180°

⇒ 2x + y = 180° --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Since **AB || CD**, ∠ARP = ∠RSC (**Corresponding angles**)

⇒ ∠RSC = 2x°

⇒ Now, at point **S**, ∠RSC + ∠DSP = 180° (**Linear pair**)

⇒ 2x + 4x = 180°

⇒ 6x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 6 = 30°

⇒ Substitute x = 30 in Equation 1:

⇒ 2(30) + y = 180°

⇒ 60 + y = 180°

⇒ y = 180° − 60° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 30; 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, angles in the same relative position at each intersection are equal.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal are equal (e.g., ∠BRS = ∠RSC).

Co-interior Angles

Interior angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary, meaning their sum is 180°.</p

Applying this to the given equations: 4/8 = b/4 = 3/c.

⇒ 1/2 = b/4 ⇒ b = 2.

⇒ 1/2 = 3/c ⇒ c = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 2, 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: 4x² + bx + 3 = 0

Equation 2: 8x² + 4x + c = 0

**Formula Used:**

For equations a₁x² + b₁x + c₁ = 0 and a₂x² + b₂x + c₂ = 0 having **common roots**:

a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

**Calculations:**

Comparing the coefficients of both equations:

⇒ 4/8 = b/4 = 3/c

Taking the first two parts to find **b**:

⇒ 4/8 = b/4

⇒ 1/2 = b/4

⇒ b = 4/2 = 2

Taking the first and third parts to find **c**:

⇒ 4/8 = 3/c

⇒ 1/2 = 3/c

⇒ c = 3 × 2 = 6

Thus, the values are b = 2 and c = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 2, 6.**

Sum and Product of Roots

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots (α + β) = −b/a and the product of roots (αβ) = c/a.

Nature of Roots

questions.question: The shorter side of a rectangle is 16 cm less than the longer side. The numerical value of its area is equal to 3 times the numerical value of its perimeter. What is the length (in cm) of its longer side?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **longer side** be L and **shorter side** be (L − 16).

Area = 3 × Perimeter ⇒ L(L − 16) = 3 × 2[L + (L − 16)]

L² − 16L = 6(2L − 16) ⇒ L² − 16L = 12L − 96

L² − 28L + 96 = 0 ⇒ (L − 24)(L − 4) = 0

Since L > 16 (as shorter side L − 16 must be positive), L = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b43df18acc6d864c27ce2aad6cc85ca722371291cf0f2f01200497253774f6f3.png] 

**Given:**

**Longer side** = L

**Shorter side** = L − 16

**Area** = L(L − 16)

**Perimeter** = 2(L + L − 16) = 2(2L − 16) = 4L − 32

**Calculations:**

⇒ L(L − 16) = 3 × (4L − 32)

⇒ L² − 16L = 12L − 96

⇒ L² − 28L + 96 = 0

⇒ L² − 24L − 4L + 96 = 0

⇒ L(L − 24) − 4(L − 24) = 0

⇒ (L − 24)(L − 4) = 0

⇒ L = 24 or L = 4

If L = 4, then Shorter side = 4 − 16 = −12 (Not possible).

⇒ L = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rectangle Mensuration

The **Area** of a rectangle is length × breadth, and the **Perimeter** is 2 × (length + breadth).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The **Diagonal** (d) is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem: d = √(L² + B²).

Quadratic Roots Property

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.</p

• The case did involve **allegations of brutal non-consensual sexual assault** by the husband on his wife.
 
• The** wife died** in this case, and her death was linked to the **sexual assault.**
 
• However, the focus of the ruling was primarily on the application of **marital rape** laws and whether the actions of the husband constituted rape, which leads us to the second statement.
 
 
 
• Contrary to the statement, the **Chhattisgarh High Court acquitted the husband**. The court **did not convict him** for rape, as it applied **Exception 2 to Section 375** of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
 
• This exception exempts a husband from being charged with rape for sexual intercourse with his wife, provided the wife is not under 15 years of age.
 
• In this case, the court ruled that **the husband could not be convicted of rape** or other charges like **unnatural sexual offenses** because of the exception in the law.

• Implications:
 
 
• The ruling has sparked debate on marital rape laws in India.
 
• It highlights the legal gap in addressing non-consensual sex in marriage, where the law still treats marital rape as legal in certain circumstances.
 
• The case points to the need for legal reforms regarding the criminalization of marital rape.
 
 

Status of Marital Rape in India:__

__
 
• Legal Position:

 
 
• Marital rape is not criminalized in India, except for cases where the wife is under the age of 15.
 
• The Indian Penal Code (IPC), under Section 375, considers marital rape legal when the wife is above 15 years of age.
 
 
 
• Debate:
 
 
• There is strong public debate and activism pushing for changes to recognize marital rape as a criminal offense.
 
• Legal experts, women’s rights groups, and the UN have called for a reform in Indian law to criminalize marital rape, but no changes have been made in the law so far.

• 2015: Supreme Court ruled that sexual intercourse with a wife below 15 years is rape.
 
• 2017: Law Commission of India recommended criminalizing marital rape, but the recommendation was not implemented.
 
• 2021: Delhi High Court raised concerns over marital rape but did not rule on the issue.
 
• Current Status:
 
 
• Despite growing calls for reform, marital rape remains not criminalized in India.

questions.question: If x + y = 14, product of x and y is 45, then the value of x⁴ + y⁴ is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find two **numbers** whose **sum** is 14 and **product** is 45.

By factoring 45: 9 × 5 = 45 and 9 + 5 = 14.

∴ x = 9 and y = 5 (or vice versa).

The required value is 9⁴ + 5⁴ = 6561 + 625 = 7186.

**∴ The correct answer is 7186.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x + y = 14 and xy = 45.

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe72a6feee04f6217d6375602598bff000cb541a4f9f259316e314a54f434b2b.png] 

⇒ (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

⇒ 14² = x² + y² + 2(45)

⇒ 196 = x² + y² + 90

⇒ x² + y² = 106

⇒ Squaring again: (x² + y²)² = x⁴ + y⁴ + 2(x²y²)

⇒ (106)² = x⁴ + y⁴ + 2(xy)²

⇒ 11236 = x⁴ + y⁴ + 2(45)²

⇒ 11236 = x⁴ + y⁴ + 2(2025)

⇒ 11236 = x⁴ + y⁴ + 4050

⇒ x⁴ + y⁴ = 11236 − 4050 = 7186

**∴ The correct answer is 7186.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Expansion

The square of a trinomial or higher powers can be derived using the **Binomial Theorem** or successive squaring of **standard identities**.

Power Product Rule

For any non-zero numbers, (ab)ⁿ = aⁿ × bⁿ. This is used to simplify terms like (xy)² as x²y².

Sum of Cubes Identity

x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² − xy + y²). Useful for finding **cubic values** when sum and product are known.</p

Identify two numbers with a **difference of 27** whose **product is 2268**.

Check options for **breadth (b)**: If b = 36, then length (l) = 36 + 27 = 63.

Product: 36 × 63 = 2268. This matches the given **area**.

⇒ b² + 63b − 36b − 2268 = 0

⇒ b(b + 63) − 36(b + 63) = 0

⇒ (b − 36)(b + 63) = 0

⇒ b = 36 or b = −63 (Length/Breadth cannot be negative)

⇒ b = 36 m

**∴ The correct answer is 36 m.**

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ASCII** stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, which is a character encoding standard for electronic communication.
 
• It assigns **numerical values** (ranging from 0 to 127) to represent characters such as **letters, digits, punctuation marks, and control characters**.
 
• The use of ASCII allows **computers and electronic devices** to communicate efficiently by representing text in a universally understood manner.
 
• **Each character** (e.g., "A", "B", "1", "!") is mapped to a unique **7-bit binary number**, making it lightweight and efficient for data processing and storage.
 
• It provides a **standardized way of encoding text**, which is essential for compatibility across different systems and applications.
 
• ASCII is widely used in **programming, data processing, and networking**, especially in systems where text representation is critical.
 
• For example, the letter "A" is represented by the **numerical value 65**, and the character "1" is represented by 49 in ASCII.
 
• Extended versions of ASCII (such as **ISO-8859-1**) include additional characters to support other languages and symbols.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 19 years more than 2 times the present age of the son. After 15 years, 12 times the father's age will be 17 years less than 13 times the son's age. The difference (in years) between the present ages of the father and the son is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the first condition: **Father** + **Son** = 2 × **Son** + 19

⇒ **Father** − **Son** = 19

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** throughout their lives.

Since the question asks for the difference between their present ages, it is directly obtained from the first equation.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd0fd3f712631713262e86bdccb47b5bacaf3e24ca04701ded37192b3917a028.png] 

Let the present age of the **Father** be F and the **Son** be S.

**Case 1:** Sum of ages is 19 more than twice the son's age.

⇒ F + S = 2S + 19

⇒ F − S = 19 .................(1)

**Case 2:** After 15 years, 12 times father's age is 17 less than 13 times son's age.

⇒ 12(F + 15) = 13(S + 15) − 17

⇒ 12F + 180 = 13S + 195 − 17

⇒ 12F − 13S = 195 − 17 − 180

⇒ 12F − 13S = −2 .................(2)

From (1), F = S + 19. Substitute in (2):

⇒ 12(S + 19) − 13S = −2

⇒ 12S + 228 − 13S = −2

⇒ −S = −230 ⇒ S = 230 (This verifies the second condition holds for specific values, but the difference is already established).

⇒ Difference = F − S = 19 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals never changes with time. If the difference is **x years** today, it will remain **x years** after **n years**.

Ratio Method for Ages

When ratios at two different times are given, equate the **unit difference** between the ratios to the **actual year gap** to find present ages quickly.</p
